MEASURED on an idle box, GNU coreutils 8.32 — 5.2.37: buildArgv 653.4 us, argv 1196.3 us, new+argv+delete 3120.6 us, bare head -n 1 34.14 ms vs take 39.40 ms = 1.15x, bare head -n 5000 36.02 ms vs take 39.97 ms = 1.10x, wc-equivalent 51.05 ms vs h.count 725.67 ms = 14.21x (~134 us/record), gates 2/2 PASS. 5.3.9: 692.2 / 1290.6 / 3199.5 us, 35.88 vs 43.19 ms = 1.20x, 33.23 vs 41.12 ms = 1.23x, 48.93 vs 731.64 ms = 14.95x (~136 us/record), gates 2/2 PASS. Both rc 0 under `bash -eu`. TWO PLAN ESTIMATES REFINED (conclusion unchanged, written into PLAN §5 and both bench headers): a whole tool run is 33-36 ms, not ~42 ms, and the wrapper's fixed delta is 3.1-3.3 ms, not ~3.9 ms; the ratio is therefore ~(34+3.2)/34 and falls as the corpus grows, which is why -n 1 and -n 5000 agree within a few percent. DEVIATION from the letter of the brief: the 007 `count` case runs over 200 records, not the bench's 5000 — the count sink's cost is PER RECORD (~135 us), so at 5000 records the idle ratio is already 14x and a 10x ceiling would fail by construction; at 200 records it is under 3x idle and the ceiling still catches an order-of-magnitude regression. The gated take shapes are unchanged at -n 1 and -n 1000 (2000-line corpus). DEVIATION from the plan letter: PLAN §2.4/§3 H7 says two 3-line files under -n 5 with the FIRST unterminated are 7 records; measured on coreutils 8.32 it is 8 (the separator's leading \n terminates the previous file's last line instead of standing alone as an empty record, so exactly ONE record is lost relative to the terminated pair's 9). Second correction: PLAN §2.5/H3 says a 19-digit count is 'an ordinary rc 1 with the tool's own message' — `head -n 9999999999999999999` is rc 0 (it fits in uintmax); the shape that really is rc 1 is `head -c -9999999999999999999` ('invalid number of bytes: Value too large'), and that is what 005 pins.
